links.outcome: Rubric score and pairwise win rates of LLMs with versus without guideline RAG grounding
links.effect: RAG raised mean rubric scores for Qwen2.5-14B (3.72 to 3.77), GPT-3.5 (+0.05), LLaMA3-8B (+0.02); decreased GPT-4-turbo (-0.04) and OpenBioLLM-8B (-0.22). Win rates improved 16%-46% for most models.
links.quote: Direct comparisons conducted by the LLM-as-a-judge show that RAG improved win rates for most models.

links.outcome: Comparison of small open-source RAG models against GPT-4-turbo and GPT-3.5 on same queries
links.effect: RAG-enhanced Qwen2.5-14B scored 3.77 vs 3.96 for GPT-4-turbo (pairwise 0.72 vs 0.81), and outperformed GPT-3.5-turbo across all metrics.
links.quote: Qwen2.5-14B outperformed GPT-3.5-turbo across all metrics, achieving a normalized pairwise score of 0.72 versus 0.81 for GPT-4-turbo.

links.outcome: Rubric score of Qwen2.5-14B across varying numbers of retrieved contexts (k=1 to 50)
links.effect: Optimal at k=5 (3.77); stable at k=1 and 3, sharp decline at k=10, reaching 1.37 at k=50 (64% decline).
links.quote: Performance remained relatively stable at k = 1 and k = 3 but experienced a sharp decline at k = 10, reaching a minimum score of 1.37 at k = 50.

links.outcome: Agreement of LLM judge with alternate LLM judge and human oncologists
links.effect: DeepSeek-V3 cross-validation Pearson r=0.876, Kendall tau=0.956; human experts scored lower than LLM judge (mean 3.81 vs 4.12) on 10 queries.
links.quote: Human experts assigned lower scores than the LLM judge across all metrics (mean 3.81 v 4.12).

links.outcome: Qualitative expert review of factual errors in RAG responses
links.effect: Nonsystematic review found errors in Qwen2.5-14B (abbreviation misinterpretation n=3, cross-indication PARP extrapolation n=1, incomplete HER2 SISH n=1) and GPT-4-turbo (incorrect denosumab citation n=1, incomplete n=1, off-topic n=1); hallucination rate not quantified.
links.quote: In GPT-4-turbo: incomplete HER2 SISH description (n = 1), incorrect denosumab citation for hypercalcemia (n = 1), and an off-topic response (n = 1).

links.outcome: Factual inaccuracies in fluent RAG-generated guideline answers requiring verification
links.effect: Expert inspection found failure modes in both models (abbreviation drift, cross-indication extrapolation, algorithmic incompleteness) despite fluent output; authors state clinician oversight is required.
links.quote: These failure modes—abbreviation drift, cross-indication extrapolation, and algorithmic incompleteness—carry patient-safety risks and underscore that RAG responses require clinician oversight even when they appear fluent and well organized.

links.outcome: Rubric and pairwise response quality with RAG
links.effect: Average scores improved GPT-3.5 +0.05, Qwen +0.05, LLaMA +0.02; decreased GPT-4 -0.04 and OpenBio -0.22; win-rate gains 16%-46%.
links.quote: Direct head-to-head comparisons demonstrate that RAG consistently improves performance for most models, with the notable exception of OpenBioLLM, confirming the general effectiveness of the RAG implementation.

links.outcome: Candidate model performance on same queries
links.effect: OpenBioLLM scored lower than Llama3: 2.69 v 3.36 with RAG; 2.92 v 3.34 without.
links.quote: OpenBioLLM-8B scored lower than its base Llama3-8B in both conditions (average 2.69 v 3.36 with RAG; 2.92 v 3.34 without) and produced markedly shorter responses (mean 401 v 1,447 characters), frequently adopting terse, single-sentence formats absent in general-purpose models.

links.effect: Qwen RAG: abbreviation errors n=3, PARP extrapolation n=1, incomplete HER2 SISH n=1.
links.quote: In Qwen2.5-14B: abbreviation misinterpretation (n = 3, eg, “PABC” incorrectly expanded as “positive axillary breast cancer”), cross-indication PARP inhibitor extrapolation (n = 1), and incomplete 2023 ASCO/CAP HER2 SISH algorithm description (n = 1).

links.effect: GPT-4-turbo RAG had incorrect denosumab citation for hypercalcemia (n = 1).
links.quote: In GPT-4-turbo: incomplete HER2 SISH description (n = 1), incorrect denosumab citation for hypercalcemia (n = 1), and an off-topic response (n = 1).

links.effect: Specialist review found Qwen failures n=5 and GPT-4 failures n=3 in RAG responses; authors state patient-safety risks.
links.quote: These failure modes—abbreviation drift, cross-indication extrapolation, and algorithmic incompleteness—carry patient-safety risks and underscore that RAG responses require clinician oversight even when they appear fluent and well organized.

unlisted_practices: Optimize and test the number of retrieved RAG context chunks, because excessive retrieved context degraded answer quality.

links.outcome: Clinical question answering performance with and without RAG
links.effect: Rubric gains ranged from 0.02 to 0.05 on a 5-point scale (with decreases for GPT-4-turbo by 0.04 and OpenBioLLM-8B by 0.22), while relative improvements in head-to-head win rates ranged from 16% to 46%.
links.quote: Although absolute rubric gains were modest (0.02-0.05 on a five-point scale), relative improvements in head-to-head win rates ranged from 16% to 46%.
